reasoning_traces.think:
The temporal cohort split operator \( \mathcal{S}_{\text{IS}} \cup \mathcal{S}_{\text{OOS}} = \mathcal{P} \) partitions a dataset into in-sample and out-of-sample subsets based on a fixed boundary date. This structure allows for empirical validation of model performance without data leakage. The Brier score \( B = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (p_i - o_i)^2 \) quantifies forecast accuracy where \( p_i \) is predicted probability and \( o_i \in \{0,1\} \) is outcome. The Brier score delta \( \Delta B = B_{\text{OOS}} - B_{\text{IS}} \) measures whether model performance degrades in the future. If \( \Delta B < 0 \), the model is more accurate in OOS, suggesting good generalization. A positive \( \Delta B \) indicates overfitting. The health assessment \( \mathcal{H}(\mathcal{S}_{\text{OOS}}) \) flags models that fail to maintain performance across time, which is critical for both GSI’s Bayesian inference and GSE’s adaptive decision logic. Failure modes include insufficient sample size, temporal shift in data distribution, or model instability.
